report.summary: Reviewed events.py chunk 1 of 1: dataclass definitions and event_to_transport_record function.
risks: event_to_transport_record | medium | Default case uses json.dumps(payload) for events not explicitly handled, which may produce unexpected output for future event types. | Add explicit handling or a test for each event type.

handoff.purpose: Define event dataclasses and the function to convert events to TransportRecord.

symbols.name: AgentCapabilities
symbols.note: Dataclass with streaming, resume, hidden_state_access flags.

symbols.name: SessionEnded
symbols.note: Dataclass with session_id, exit_code, stderr fields.

symbols.name: ToolRequested
symbols.note: Dataclass with tool_name, arguments, call_id fields.

symbols.name: ToolCompleted
symbols.note: Dataclass with call_id, result, is_error fields.

symbols.name: CommandOutput
symbols.note: Dataclass with command, output, exit_code fields.

symbols.name: AgentEvent
symbols.note: Union type of all event dataclasses.

symbols.name: TransportRecord
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for lossless envelope; includes to_dict, from_dict, embedding_text methods.

symbols.name: event_to_transport_record
symbols.note: Converts an AgentEvent to a TransportRecord with given session_id, runtime, direction, sequence, optional metadata.

claims.text: Lossless envelope exchanged between a runtime shell and downstream sinks.
claims.why: TransportRecord contains all fields from the original event plus metadata; to_dict/from_dict preserve data.

claims.text: Embeddings are derived from this record; they never replace its original payload or provenance.
claims.why: embedding_text returns a string derived from the record; payload and metadata remain unchanged.

claims.text: Stable text projection used by an optional embedding index.
claims.why: The method returns a formatted string combining runtime, direction, event_type, and content.

claims.text: Wrap one typed event without discarding its provider-neutral payload.
claims.why: The function converts an AgentEvent to TransportRecord, preserving the event's payload in the payload field.

claims.text: direction must be input, output, or system
claims.why: The function raises ValueError if direction is not in {'input', 'output', 'system'}.

observations.what: Default content generation uses json.dumps(payload) for events not explicitly handled, which may produce unexpected output for future event types.
